chapters.english_title: A Choice That Has a Cost: A Signal
chapters.chinese_title: 有代价的选择：一个信号
chapters.theme: 心理、决策、责任与人生选择
english_paragraphs: They had published every exemption and still lost the room; now the only question left was what each of them would choose. The tenth arc began in a museum of urban history, where the choice of a career seemed to require an assessment that nobody had written. “A birth in a village and a degree in the city do not produce the same consciousness,” the director said. “You have a steady record and a supreme reputation, and now you must decide what it is for.”

The dilemma was polite and fierce at once. “I appreciate the offer,” Lin said, “but an elegant title is not the same as integrity.” A prospective employer had sent a memo and a memorandum about the modernization of the plant; a second letter mentioned its modernisation in the same breath, and a third asked about neutrality in a dispute the plant had already lost.

The wildlife survey was the reminder of what the group actually owned: a decent dataset, a doubtful forecast, and a dying weather station. “A reversal of the verdict would require a decisive report,” Maya wrote. “We can imitate a respectable process and we cannot fake the perseverance behind it.”

The puzzle of the second week was the acidity of the river. “A permissive rule and a corrupt reading have the same effect on a sample,” the analyst said. “The difference is who signs it.” Her willpower had carried the survey through a coarse season, and the group had not noticed.

The reproductive data and the urbanisation figures arrived on the same morning. “We urbanise a district and we call it growth,” the planner said. “To urbanize is not the same as to improve.” The hesitation in the room was honest, and it was the first useful signal of the whole arc.

The insanity of the summer had been the attempt to do both jobs, and the healthy response was to let one of them go. “A fire in the building would not require less of us,” the director said. “It would require the same people, now, with a true answer.” It was a pleasant fortune, and it did not appear by accident. We had to guess how the production of a survey could fill the role of a job, and we could avoid the fall only by refusing to sell the museum's data. A sincere sorry would not do; a quiet defiance would.
chinese_paragraphs: 他们已经公布了每一份豁免，却仍然失去了那间屋子；如今剩下的唯一问题是，他们各自会选择什么。第十段弧线开始于一座城市历史博物馆，在那里，职业的选择似乎需要一份没人写过的评估。“出生在村庄和在城市获得学位，并不会产生同样的意识，”主管说，“你有一份稳定的履历和一个至高的名声，现在你必须决定它是为了什么。”
这个困境既有礼貌又凶猛。“我感激这份邀约，”林伟说，“但一个优雅的头衔不等于正直。”一位潜在的雇主寄来一份备忘录和一份关于工厂现代化的备忘文件；第二封信在同一口气里提到了它的另一种拼法；第三封信问的是在一场工厂已经输掉的争议中的中立。
野生动物调查提醒了他们真正拥有什么：一份尚可的数据集、一份可疑的预报，以及一座垂死的气象站。“要翻转这个裁决，需要一份果断的报告，”曼雅写道，“我们可以模仿一个体面的流程，却无法伪造它背后的毅力。”
第二周的难题是河流的酸性。“一条纵容的规则和一次腐败的读法，对样本产生同样的影响，”分析师说，“区别在于谁签的字。”她的意志力让这项调查撑过了一个粗糙的季节，而小组没有注意到。
生殖数据与城市化数字在同一个早上到来。“我们把一个区都市化，然后称之为增长，”规划者说，“使都市化不等于改善。”屋里那份犹豫是诚实的，而它是整段弧线第一个有用的信号。
这个夏天的荒唐之处在于想同时做两份工作，而健康的回应是放掉其中一份。“楼里着火不会要求我们更少，”主管说，“它会要求同样这些人，在此时此刻，给出一个真实的答案。”这是一份令人愉快的运气，而它不是偶然出现的。我们必须猜测，一份调查的生产如何才能填满一份工作的角色，而只有拒绝出售博物馆的数据，我们才能避开那次跌落。一句真诚的道歉没有用；一次安静的蔑视才有用。

chapters.english_title: A Choice That Has a Cost: The First Promise
chapters.chinese_title: 有代价的选择：第一次承诺
chapters.theme: 心理、决策、责任与人生选择
english_paragraphs: The first promise was made at the graduation ceremony, in the cold of a western winter: each graduate would publish one chapter of the group's history. “The goal is not the size of the report,” the director said at the meeting, “it is the duty to hand over the primary record.”

The average reader of the index would never see the distribution of the evidence, and that was the point. “A dead archive is a kind of lie,” Maya said. “A present-tense account is a kind of evidence.” The spirit of the assignment was to write down the origin of every number, including the ones with a fault.

The moment of conversion came with a photograph. “This image is identical to the one in the party's leaflet,” Lin said. “We have tied our history to a political leaflet, and we did not notice.” The stake was not money but the taste of the whole project.

The rough draft of the fifth chapter had a tie to an antique map and a reserve of unprocessed field notes. “A trick of presentation will not save a weak index,” the director said. “A sacrifice is required, and it is the sacrifice of the pretty sentence.”

The confusion in the room was about ownership. “Only ten of us wrote it, and even the town has a claim,” the editor said. “We cannot cling to a private sphere and call it public scholarship.” The reward for publishing was, in the end, the release itself.

A faint frost on the window, a stroke of the pen, and the preview of the last page: the promise was convert into a series of small assignments, and the convertible one was the only one the group could honestly sign. The ten of us met then, and the section on the party was the hardest. A type of town, a certain world, a town that would not die: the evidence was political even when we said that it was not. We had to show the break in the record and let the reader see it, and only the town could decide what to publish. The present page would seem to choke on its own inclination.
chinese_paragraphs: 第一个承诺是在毕业典礼上做出的，在一个西方冬天的寒冷里：每位毕业生将公开这个小组历史中的一章。“目标不是报告的规模，”主管在会上说，“而是移交第一手记录的责任。”
索引的普通读者永远不会看到证据的分布，而重点正在这里。“一座死的档案是一种谎言，”曼雅说，“一份现在时态的记述是一种证据。”这项任务的精神是写下每一个数字的来源，包括那些有毛病的。
转变的时刻随着一张照片到来。“这张影像与那份党传单上的一模一样，”林伟说，“我们把我们的历史系在了一份政治传单上，而我们没有注意到。”赌注不是钱，而是整个项目的情调。
第五章的粗略草稿与一张古董地图和一批未整理的野外笔记有关。“呈现上的一个诀窍救不了一个虚弱的索引，”主管说，“需要一种牺牲，而它就是牺牲那句漂亮的句子。”
屋里的混乱是关于归属的。“只有我们十个人写了它，而连镇上也有份，”编辑说，“我们不能紧抓着一个私人领域，然后称之为公共学术。”公开的报酬，说到底，就是那次公开本身。
窗上一层淡淡的霜、笔的一划，以及最后一页的预览：这个承诺被转换成一连串小任务，而可转换的那一个，是小组唯一能诚实地签下的一个。我们十个人那时聚在一起，而关于那个党的那一节最难写。一种城镇、一个特定的世界、一个不会死去的城镇：即使我们说它不是政治的，这些证据也是政治的。我们必须展示记录中的断裂，并让读者看见它，而只有那个镇能决定公布什么。眼前这一页似乎会被自己的倾向噎住。

chapters.english_title: A Choice That Has a Cost: A Missing Voice
chapters.chinese_title: 有代价的选择：缺席的声音
chapters.theme: 心理、决策、责任与人生选择
english_paragraphs: The missing voice belonged to a clown at the children's ceremony during the settlement week. “You never asked the age of the people who will live under this roof,” he said. “You have a purpose and a vote, and you have not asked whether the house is impossible to heat.”

The apparent answer was attractive: select a smaller unit, choose a cautious price, and forget the rest. “Sorrow is not a clinical condition,” he said, “and a guidance note is not counsel.” A stir in the hall made the identification of the real problem evident: there was no equality in the plan.

The equality he meant was measured in decades. “A materialist reads a house as an asset,” he said. “A materialist should also read it as a lifetime.” His idealism, he admitted, was cheerful and his realism was not; the seeming contradiction was the whole of his argument.

The solidity of the building was never in doubt, and the eternity of a mortgage was. “You can visualize a family in it, and you cannot visualize a family paying for it,” he said. “A clear-cut plan would say who repays and when.”

The blame for the confusion lay with the guidance, not with the family. “A cautious buyer and a cheating seller can look alike on paper,” Maya wrote. “The difference is the second page.” The voice he raised was mad by their standards and just by his own.

The settlement was revised by one clause: every unit would be sold with a heating assessment attached. It was almost nothing, and it was nearly everything, and the group agreed to appear at the next meeting with the figure. They agreed almost at once, and I nearly said nothing. We need a similar kind of free claim, and a true history is not a chapter that dies. A kind moment, an image, and a win were not enough while nearly half the residents were absent. The break in the plan appeared as a missing page, and almost everyone who could vote did; the need was similar to the earlier survey. We must decide whether the dead govern us; a house is alive in a way that materialism cannot visualise, and the death of the old plan did not settle the question. The settlement would visualise the cost instead.
chinese_paragraphs: 那个缺席的声音属于安置周期间儿童典礼上的一个小丑。“你们从来没有问过将要住在这个屋顶下的人的年龄，”他说，“你们有一个目的和一次表决，而你们没有问过这栋房子是不是无法取暖。”
表面的答案是吸引人的：选一个更小的单元、挑一个谨慎的价格，其余的忘掉。“悲伤不是一种临床状态，”他说，“一份指导说明不是法律顾问。”大厅里的一阵骚动让真正问题的身份变得明显：这份方案里没有平等。
他所说的平等是以十年为单位计量的。“唯物主义者把房子读成一项资产，”他说，“唯物主义者也应该把它读成一辈子。”他承认，他的理想主义是欢快的，而他的现实主义不是；这个表面上的矛盾就是他论证的全部。
这栋楼的坚固性从未被怀疑，而被怀疑的是一笔按揭的永恒。“你可以在里面想象一个家庭，却无法想象一个家庭在付它的钱，”他说，“一份明确的方案会说明谁偿还、何时偿还。”
混乱该归咎于那份指导，而不是那个家庭。“一个谨慎的买家和一个作弊的卖家在纸上看起来可以很像，”曼雅写道，“区别在第二页。”他提高的嗓音按他们的标准是疯狂的，按他自己的标准是公正的。

安置方案因一条条款而被修改：每个单元出售时都必须附一份取暖评估。这几乎什么都不是，也几乎就是一切，而小组同意带着这个数字出现在下次会议上。他们几乎立刻就同意了，而我几乎什么也没说。我们需要一种类似的、自由的诉求，而一部真实的历史不是一章会死去的东西。在将近一半居民缺席的时候，一个善意的时刻、一张图像和一场胜利都不够。方案里的断裂以一张缺页的形式出现，而几乎所有能投票的人都投了；这种需要与早先那次调查相似。我们必须决定死者是否在统治我们；一栋房子是活的，其方式唯物主义无法想象，而旧计划的死亡并没有解决这个问题。这份安置方案将转而把代价想象出来。

chapters.english_title: A Choice That Has a Cost: Evidence on the Table
chapters.chinese_title: 有代价的选择：摆上桌面的证据
chapters.theme: 心理、决策、责任与人生选择
english_paragraphs: The evidence meeting was held tonight because the news could not wait, and the argument on the table was about a defective pearl. “I believe the report and I cannot approve it,” the auditor said. “Everything upon it rests on one page, and that page was written prior to the test.”

The dispute concerning the twentieth chapter was simple: accept the figure or deny it. “You insist that we respond tonight,” Lin said. “I would rather remind you that a compelling thesis can still be wrong.” A generous reader would argue the same point, and a cop at the door would not.

The group had promised not to pretend. “We will declare the error and we will not seize the moment to look good,” Maya wrote. “Onto every page we will put the name of the person who checked it, and okay means checked.”

The prior year had been wound backwards: a nightly habit of re-doing each report, an entrepreneurial push that frightened the volunteers, and a forgetful editor who had misplaced one page. “Weep if you like,” the auditor said, “but stabilize the process first.”

The surrounding argument was about the underwear factory and the couple who owned it. “It is too easy to rob a small firm of its name,” Lin said. “A fine is not the same as a fair verdict, and an exception is not a rule.”

The choice of the twentieth chapter was to publish everything except the private correspondence, and to try the whole record against the purpose it claimed. “A generous account is not a flattering one,” the auditor said, and the meeting closed without an argument. Age is different from death, and during the year we decided to keep every point about the effect. The fine was never news, the purpose was never just, and the couple who built it seemed to be under a different sky. The choice was to decide during the same meeting, and to choose the harder option; it was never only about the fine, and the news, the point, and the effect were the same as before. Although we cannot swear to every page, we welcome the check, and we will not entertain a version that hides it.
chinese_paragraphs: 证据会议在今晚召开，因为消息等不了，而桌上的争论关乎一颗有缺陷的珍珠。“我相信这份报告，但我无法批准它，”审计员说，“它之上的一切都依赖一页纸，而那一页是在测试之前写的。”
关于第二十章的争论很简单：接受这个数字，或者否认它。“你坚持要我们今晚回应，”林伟说，“我更愿意提醒你，一篇有说服力的论文仍然可能是错的。”一位慷慨的读者会提出同样的观点，而门口那位警察不会。
小组承诺过不假装。“我们会声明这个错误，也不会抓住这个时机让自己好看，”曼雅写道，“在每一页上，我们都会写上核对者的名字，而‘可以’的意思就是已核对。”
前一年是被倒着缠回去的：每晚重做每份报告的习气、一次吓得志愿者发抖的创业式推进，以及一位把某一页放错了地方的健忘编辑。“你想哭就哭吧，”审计员说，“但请先把流程稳住。”
外围的争论关乎那家内衣厂和拥有它的那对夫妇。“太容易就剥夺一家小公司的名声了，”林伟说，“一笔罚款不等于一个公正的裁决，而一个例外不是一条规则。”

第二十章的选择是：除了私人通信以外全部公开，并尝试用整份记录去检验它所声称的目的。“一份慷慨的记述不是一份谄媚的记述，”审计员说，而会议在没有争执的情况下结束。年龄不同于死亡，而在这一年里我们决定保留关于那个影响的每一个要点。那笔罚款从来不是新闻，那个目的从来不是公正的，而建造它的那对夫妇似乎生活在另一片天空下。这个选择是在同一次会议上作出决定，并选择更难的那个选项；它从来不只关乎那笔罚款，而新闻、那个要点以及那个影响，都和从前一样。虽然我们无法为每一页发誓，但我们欢迎这次核对，也不会去迎合一个把它藏起来的版本。
